claim: S1: Transformer architecture supports parallelizable sequence modelling.
notes: Architecture predecessor; not evidence about RAG value or Chinese/English product accuracy.

claim: S2: BART introduced denoising pretraining for sequence-to-sequence generation.
notes: Generation predecessor; its benchmark results do not establish this application.

claim: S3: DPR used learned dense representations to retrieve passages.
notes: Retrieval predecessor; relevance is not document authority or approval.

claim: S4: RAG combined a pretrained generator with external retrieval for knowledge-intensive generation.
notes: Methods sections 2.2 and 2.3 identify DPR and BART: https://arxiv.org/html/2005.11401v4 . Original fine-tuned RAG differs from a modern retrieve-then-prompt workflow. This is a milestone, not the origin of all retrieval-assisted NLP.

claim: S5: Tested models were sensitive to the position of relevant information in long contexts.
notes: Contrary evidence: supplying information does not ensure it is used correctly. Does not establish failure rates of all present-day models.

claim: S6: Provider documentation describes retrieval and generation from proprietary sources, including citations.
notes: Evidence of packaged provider support, not independent reliability, adoption prevalence, ROI, or vendor selection advice.
